indescribable

/in-dih-SKY-buh-bul/ — stress on SKY · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Indescribable describes something so extreme that ordinary words cannot fully capture it.

Her relief when the lost puppy finally trotted home was indescribable.

Example

When she opened the door and saw the handmade quilt her grandmother had made 50 years ago, her emotions were indescribable.

in (not) + describe + able (can be done) = cannot be described. The mingling of joy, grief, and gratitude exceeded what words could capture.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

beyond words: Beyond words is the casual, everyday phrase — the thing you'd say aloud after a concert. Indescribable packs the same claim into a single, more formal word that fits essays and reports. Both say language cannot capture the thing; only indescribable is at home in formal writing.

inexpressible: Inexpressible almost always describes inner feelings — grief, relief, sudden joy — that a person cannot put into words, and its tone is quieter, flatter. Indescribable is wider and more vivid, fitting sights and experiences as naturally as emotions. A sunset can be indescribable; the ache of missing someone is inexpressible.

ineffable: Ineffable means too great for words, with an air of the sacred or mystical hanging about it — mystics call visions of the divine ineffable. Indescribable is the plainer, more forceful cousin: it says language fails without suggesting holiness. A roller-coaster drop can be indescribable; a saint's vision is ineffable.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

describable: able to be captured in words

unremarkable: ordinary and easy to sum up

Where it sits · how far it goes beyond words

striking → remarkable → breathtaking → indescribable

striking vs. indescribable: A striking sunset catches your eye for a moment, but an indescribable one leaves you unable to find any words at all.

remarkable vs. indescribable: A remarkable view is worth telling your friends about; an indescribable view defeats every attempt to tell them.

breathtaking vs. indescribable: A breathtaking scene stuns you briefly, while an indescribable scene goes past what language can even hold.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-: not (Latin)

Root — describ(e): to write down, put into words (from Latin describere, scribere 'to write') (Latin)

Suffix — -able: can be done (Latin)

Put it together: In- (not) + describe + -able (can be done) builds the meaning literally: something that cannot be described, because ordinary words fall short. Note the spelling: describe drops its final e before -able.

Use the root in a new word: description: Her description of the storm was so vivid that we could almost hear the thunder.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / literary

Use indescribable for feelings, sights, or experiences so intense or complex that ordinary adjectives fail. It's stronger than 'hard to describe' — it suggests the thing is genuinely beyond language.
